residual_risk: Fix verified via unit tests with faked /proc and injected clock/uptime values, not on an actual WSL2 machine (this sandbox is plain Linux) — the reported scenario's exact numbers (os.uptime()=2054.62s, mtime 10min 'before' derived boot) are reproduced as a test case and pass.
macOS kern.boottime path (parseKernBoottimeSec + sysctl invocation) is implemented but untested against a real Darwin machine.
Several other wiki pages (architecture/overview, concepts/worker-identity, etc.) were already stale before this task from unrelated in-flight work; left untouched as out of scope.

results.summary: Fixed the WSL2 pid-staleness false positive: pidFileStale now prefers a kernel-reported boot instant (btime/kern.boottime) via bootInstantMs, but the real fix is corroboration — pidClaimStale/cmdlineIsOurs (src/model.js) only trust a stale verdict once it's checked against /proc/<pid>/cmdline; a live pid whose cmdline still names our own `hkb dispatch --loop`/`hkb serve` is believed regardless of the arithmetic, while a live pid that does not match stays refused (keeps #202's reused-pid direction failing closed). Corroboration never manufactures staleness the timestamp verdict didn't already reach, so a pid file already fresh by arithmetic is never even checked against /proc. The change lives entirely inside readPidFile (src/board.js), so processState, the dispatcher's singleton lock, the server's claim, and hkb up's spawn gate are all fixed without any of them changing. Wiki page docs/wiki/features/up-and-down.md updated and re-stamped; docs/wiki/log.md appended. Opened draft PR #213.
